questions.prompt: In def say_hello(name):, what is name?
questions.explain: A parameter is the name in the def line. It is a placeholder that gets its value when the function is called.
An argument is the actual value handed over at the call. The parameter is the name that receives it.

questions.prompt: def add(a, b): is called as add(2). What happens?
choices: The function runs with only a
questions.explain: A parameter with no default has to be given a value. Python refuses the call rather than inventing one, which is how a missing argument gets noticed early.

questions.prompt: Match each term to what it describes.
right: the value passed in when the function is used
the name listed in the def line
writing the function name with parentheses to run it
questions.explain: Parameters are written once, in the def. Arguments are written every time you call. The call is the act of running it.
